models.title: Consumer surplus from total willingness to pay and expenditure
models.summary: Consumer surplus is the difference between willingness to pay for purchased units and the amount actually paid.

relationship.original_equation: Consumer surplus = total value - total expenditure
relationship.locator: Section 3.5: 3-5-demand-supply-and-efficiency; exact subsection stated in evidence
relationship.translation_notes: Currency minus currency yields currency. For a downward linear inverse demand with interceptA and priceP, CS=(A-P)*Q/2; this geometric specialization follows the definition and is documented without a duplicate record. For the first reference, the geometric result625 independently checks the residual. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Monetary value received beyond actual expenditure
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship
variables.domain: Nonnegative finite surplus under voluntary purchase profile

assumptions: Source assumption: total willingness to pay and expenditure concern the same bundle and consumer/market.
Application profile: voluntary purchases have V>=E; negative residuals signal an inconsistent bundle or valuation profile.
limitations: A general demand-curve area requires integration not supplied by this scalar record. Linear demand gives a triangle as an explicitly qualified closed-form profile.

models.title: Total willingness to pay across discrete acquired units
models.summary: Total consumption value adds the marginal valuations of the units in the purchased bundle.

relationship.original_equation: Total value = sum of marginal values of each acquired unit
relationship.locator: Section 3.5: 3-5-demand-supply-and-efficiency; exact subsection stated in evidence
relationship.translation_notes: All entries have currency dimension; sum preserves currency. No elementwise family arithmetic or implicit discretization of a continuous demand curve. This is total consumption valuation, distinct from V1 cash-flow additivity whose entries are dated financial cash flows. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

variables.definition: Family of monetary marginal willingness-to-pay values for the separately acquired units, each entry representing its whole unit
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Total monetary willingness to pay for all entries in the acquired-unit bundle
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Source assumption: family contains every acquired unit once; valuations are defined on the same demand ordering and monetary basis.
Application profile: finite discrete units, with each entry a complete marginal value rather than a unit price awaiting a quantity multiplier.
limitations: External binding must enforce nonnegative individual values and correct unit order; scalar guards cannot inspect family elements. Continuous-valued goods require a justified integral or analytic area instead.

models.title: Concentration ratio for an externally selected set of largest firms
models.summary: A concentration ratio combines market shares of a specified set of largest firms in the relevant market.

relationship.original_equation: Concentration ratio = combined market shares of the selected largest firms
relationship.locator: Section 11.1: 11-1-corporate-mergers; exact subsection stated in evidence
relationship.translation_notes: Shares are decimal base fractions and output is a fraction. Percentage display is handled outside the formula. Summing the externally selected shares does not identify all-market concentration distribution. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

variables.definition: Externally ranked selected largest-firm sales shares in one defined market, each as a base fraction
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship
variables.domain: 1-256 finite fractions in[0,1]; selected sum at most1

variables.definition: Fraction of total market sales represented by the supplied largest firms
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Source assumption: all firms share the same market boundary, market-share metric and observation period.
Application profile: ranking and selection are performed externally; the family includes only the specified largest firms.
limitations: No automatic sorting or industry-definition inference; element ranges and largest-firm status require external validation.

models.title: Herfindahl-Hirschman concentration on base-fraction shares
models.summary: HHI adds the squared shares of market firms and increases when sales become more concentrated.

relationship.original_equation: HHI = sum of squared market shares
relationship.locator: Definition and four-firm 30,30,20,20 percent example, first two paragraphs
relationship.translation_notes: No elementwise family arithmetic is supported, so pre-squared terms are explicit inputs. Fractions are canonical; traditional HHI points equal the index times10000 for display only and that scale is not inlined in the expression. Different share distributions can have the same HHI. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.
